reason: I want to start replacing worn blood cells; the spleen picture shows its cells taking them apart, and the intro says their iron can be reused.
expectation: I expect the spleen's cells to break down the worn cells and recover some material, possibly iron for the marrow.

alternatives.reason: The dividing base layer could also replace shedding skin, but I want to follow the blood-cell recycling route first.

effect: The spleen recovered iron from the old cells, so I can follow it to the bone marrow.
reaction: It's satisfying to see material from worn cells reused.
reason: The intro says marrow makes new blood cells and can reuse the recovered iron.
expectation: I expect the marrow to use the iron in making new red blood cells, though I don't know exactly what the next result will show.

alternatives.reason: Replacing shedding skin also fits a goal, but I want to continue the iron route first.

effect: The marrow makes replacement red cells that enter the blood, while some original-looking cells remain.
reaction: It is interesting to see both replacement and a continuing source of cells.
reason: The skin still needs a way to replace its shedding outer cells; the picture shows the base cells dividing.
expectation: I expect new cells from the base layer to move into the protective layers and replace cells shed from the surface.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the marrow to the body also seems useful, but I want to complete the skin replacement goal first.

effect: The skin stays covered as new cells move outward and specialize, and both renewal processes now need connecting to the body.
reaction: The continuous layers make the replacement process clear.
reason: I want to connect the replacement blood cells to the body, following the new goal.
expectation: I expect the body to gain a continuing supply of replacement red blood cells; the skin renewal may still need connecting afterward.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the renewing skin also fits the goal, but I chose to connect the marrow first.

effect: The body now has marrow releasing replacement red cells into its blood; the renewing skin remains to be connected.
reaction: The pelvis cutaway makes the connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it connects the renewing skin to the body.
expectation: I expect a body model showing both red blood cell replacement and skin renewal.

effect: The completed body shows both skin renewal and replacement red blood cells happening while the body stays intact.
reaction: Seeing both processes together was a satisfying ending.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following recovered iron into the marrow was most worthwhile: it connected worn-out blood cells to the making of replacements.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the marrow to the body felt mostly like an assembly step after its role was already clear.

surprise.text: I was interested that the marrow picture showed some original-looking cells remaining while new red cells entered the blood.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The final skin connection was the only offered combination, but its purpose was clear.

continue.text: I might continue if another chapter offered a similarly clear connection, though the final assembly steps felt predictable.
